title: Healthy Lifestyle 1: Nutrients and Food Tests
subject: Biology
description: The seven parts of a balanced diet, what each one does, and how to test foods for starch, lipids, sugar and protein.
author: L.M.

cards.front: What is a nutrient?
cards.back:
A substance your body needs to survive and stay healthy

(We get most of our nutrients from food.)

cards.front: What is a balanced diet?
cards.back:
Eating food with the right nutrients in the correct amounts

(Eat different foods from the different food groups, in the right amounts.)

cards.front: Name the 7 things a healthy diet needs.
cards.back: Carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, vitamins, minerals, water and fibre

cards.front: What is the function of carbohydrates?
cards.back:
Provide energy

(They are your MAIN source of energy.)

cards.front: Why do starchy foods release energy more slowly than sugary foods?
cards.back:
Starch has to be broken down by the body first

(Sugary foods like fruit give quick energy. Starchy foods like pasta and bread release it slowly.)

cards.front: Give an example of a carbohydrate-rich food.
cards.back: Pasta / bread

cards.front: What is another name for lipids?
cards.back: Fats and oils

cards.front: What are the 3 jobs of lipids?
cards.back:
Store energy, insulate the body, protect organs

(A layer under the skin keeps you warm, and lipids protect organs like the kidneys and heart from damage.)

cards.front: Give an example of a lipid-rich food.
cards.back: Fish / nuts

cards.front: What is the function of proteins?
cards.back:
Growth and repair

(They repair body tissues and make new cells. Muscles, organs and the immune system are mostly made of protein.)

cards.front: Give an example of a protein-rich food.
cards.back: Meat

cards.front: What is the function of vitamins and minerals?
cards.back:
Keep you healthy

(You only need tiny amounts.)

cards.front: Which vitamin is needed for good eyesight?
cards.back: Vitamin A

cards.front: Vitamin D works with which mineral to keep teeth and bones healthy?
cards.back: Calcium

cards.front: Which foods are a good source of vitamins and minerals?
cards.back: Fruit and vegetables

cards.front: What is the function of water in the body?
cards.back:
Needed in all cells and body fluids

(Your cells are about 70% water.)

cards.front: List four ways your body loses water.
cards.back:
Sweat, urine, faeces, breathing out

(Tears count too.)

cards.front: How much water should you drink every day?
cards.back:
Over a litre

(Tea, fruit juice and squash also count.)

cards.front: What is the function of fibre?
cards.back:
Adds bulk to food to keep it moving through the gut

(This helps prevent constipation.)

cards.front: Is fibre a nutrient?
cards.back:
No

(It is a type of carbohydrate but not classed as a nutrient. It is still important for a healthy diet.)

cards.front: Give an example of a fibre-rich food.
cards.back: Wholegrain bread / potatoes / vegetables

cards.front: What type of diet does the 'eatwell' plate help people plan?
cards.back: A balanced diet

cards.front: Why do scientists use food tests?
cards.back: To find out which nutrients are in a food

cards.front: How do you make a food solution?
cards.back:
Crush the food, add a few drops of water and mix

(Crush it with a pestle and mortar and use distilled water.)

cards.front: Which equipment do you use to crush food for a food test?
cards.back: Pestle and mortar

cards.front: What is distilled water?
cards.back: Pure water with no other chemical substances in it

cards.front: Which chemical do you use to test for starch?
cards.back: Iodine (solution)

cards.front: Starch test: what colour does iodine turn if starch is present?
cards.back:
Blue-black / black

(Iodine starts orange-yellow.)

cards.front: Which chemical do you use to test a food solution for lipids?
cards.back: Ethanol

cards.front: Lipid test: what do you see if lipids are present?
cards.back:
Cloudy

(Ethanol starts clear. Add it to the food solution, shake, leave for one minute, then pour into a test tube of water.)

cards.front: How can you test a solid piece of food for lipids?
cards.back:
Rub it on filter paper: it goes translucent if lipids are present

(Hold the paper up to the light to check.)

cards.front: Which chemical do you use to test for sugar?
cards.back: Benedict's solution

cards.front: Sugar test: what colour does Benedict's solution turn if sugar is present?
cards.back:
Orange-red / orange

(Benedict's solution starts blue.)

cards.front: Which food test needs heating in a water bath?
cards.back: The sugar test (Benedict's solution)

cards.front: Which chemicals do you use to test for protein?
cards.back: Biuret (copper sulfate and sodium hydroxide)

cards.front: Protein test: what colour do you see if protein is present?
cards.back:
Purple

(Copper sulfate solution starts pale blue.)

cards.front: What is a hypothesis?
cards.back:
An idea that explains what scientists observe

(A hypothesis can be tested in an investigation and used to make a prediction.)

questions.question: Which nutrient is the body's main source of energy?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are your main source of energy. Lipids also provide energy.

questions.question: Which nutrient is used for growth and repair?
questions.explanation: Proteins repair body tissues and make new cells for growth.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a job of lipids?
questions.explanation: Repairing tissues is the job of proteins. Lipids store energy, insulate and protect organs.

questions.question: What does fibre do?
options: Adds bulk to keep food moving through the gut
questions.explanation: Fibre adds bulk to food so it keeps moving through the gut, which helps prevent constipation.

questions.question: Vitamin D works with calcium to keep which parts of the body healthy?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D is needed with the mineral calcium for healthy teeth and bones.

questions.question: Roughly how much of a cell is water?
questions.explanation: Your cells are made up of about 70% water.

questions.question: What does a balanced diet mean?
options: Eating the right nutrients in the correct amounts
Eating the same amount of every food
questions.explanation: A balanced diet means eating food with the right nutrients in the correct amounts.

questions.question: Which chemical is used to test for starch?
questions.explanation: Iodine solution turns from orange-yellow to blue-black if starch is present.

questions.question: A food solution turns cloudy in the ethanol test. Which nutrient does it contain?
questions.explanation: Ethanol goes cloudy when lipids are present.

questions.question: What colour does Benedict's solution turn if sugar is present?
questions.explanation: Benedict's solution starts blue and turns orange-red when heated with sugar.

questions.question: Which food test needs a water bath?
questions.explanation: In the sugar test you heat the test tube with Benedict's solution in a water bath.

questions.question: What colour shows that protein is present in the Biuret test?
questions.explanation: Copper sulfate and sodium hydroxide (Biuret) turn purple if protein is present.

questions.question: Rubbing a crisp on filter paper makes the paper translucent. What does this show?
questions.explanation: Filter paper going translucent is the test for lipids in a solid food.

questions.question: What should you use to crush food when making a food solution?
questions.explanation: Crush the food with a pestle and mortar, then add a few drops of distilled water and mix.

questions.question: Which statement about fibre is true?
options: It is a type of protein
It is a carbohydrate but not a nutrient
It is a type of lipid
questions.explanation: Fibre is a type of carbohydrate but is not classed as a nutrient. It is still important for a healthy diet.

questions.question: Which of these is a good source of vitamins and minerals?
questions.explanation: Fruit and vegetables are a good source of vitamins and minerals.
